title: Identity-theft recovery and credit freezes
body_md:
## Identity recovery is a series of separate disputes

An exposed name or identity number is not the same as a fraudulent account. First establish what was exposed and what was used. A breach notice may justify protective steps even before misuse. An unfamiliar account, debt notice, tax filing or benefit claim needs a specific dispute with the organization involved. Keep records of each case and its outcome. A tax, benefits or medical-insurance misuse needs contact with that specific agency or insurer; a credit freeze does not repair it.

### US: a freeze, report and disputes

In the US, a free security freeze at **each** of Equifax, Experian and TransUnion restricts access to the credit report for new credit. It does not stop use of existing accounts, all forms of identity misuse, or every lender outside that system. You can lift it for a legitimate application. A fraud alert asks lenders to verify identity but does not block report access; an initial alert at one bureau is shared with the others. The FTC's IdentityTheft.gov produces a tailored report and recovery plan when misuse occurs. Review your credit reports, contact the issuer of each account you did not open, and dispute incorrect entries with the bureau and furnishing business. Save written confirmations. A police report may be useful in a particular process, but it is not a universal prerequisite.

### Do not export US rules

The UK, EU, UAE and other systems do not all have the US three-bureau freeze. Check local bureau, lender and identity-authority procedures. In Russia, the Bank of Russia documents a **self-ban on certain consumer loans**, available through Gosuslugi or MFC, with exclusions including mortgages and some secured or education loans. It is not identical to a US credit freeze and does not block use of an existing credit card. Use the official service to inspect its current status and terms.

If someone used your existing card or bank account, report that to the institution immediately; an identity measure cannot undo the transaction. A genuine credit application you made may be delayed by a freeze or ban, so plan a temporary lift through the official process. Avoid paid “identity repair” promises that claim a guaranteed result. Recovery ends when each fraudulent record is resolved and the protective controls you chose are documented, not after a fixed number of months.

widget_config.goal: Distinguish exposure from misuse and use the correct local protective and dispute process without treating a US freeze as universal.
widget_config.today_action: If in the US, locate the official freeze pages for all three bureaus; elsewhere, identify your local credit-report and lender-dispute routes without entering personal data into this lesson.
widget_config.scope: US freeze/FTC procedures and Russian consumer-loan self-ban are jurisdiction-specific; other countries require local checks.

blocks.title: A new card after a data breach
blocks.situation: Synthetic: an American reader receives a breach notice, then finds a credit card she never opened on her report.
blocks.analysis: She freezes each US bureau to reduce new-credit risk, reports misuse at IdentityTheft.gov, contacts the issuer and disputes the report entry. The freeze does not remove the existing fraudulent account; that needs its own dispute.

blocks.title: A legitimate mortgage application
blocks.situation: Synthetic: Omar froze his US reports months ago. A mortgage lender now says it cannot pull a report for his application.
blocks.analysis: The freeze is working as designed, not evidence of new fraud. Omar verifies the lender through a known channel, learns which bureau it uses, temporarily lifts that freeze and restores it afterward.

blocks.title: A report you did not expect
blocks.setup: Synthetic: you live in the US. A credit report shows an unfamiliar store card; an email also advertises paid “instant identity repair.”

choices.text: Place free freezes with all three US nationwide bureaus.
choices.consequence: Access to those reports for new credit is restricted.
choices.explanation: One bureau's freeze does not automatically freeze the other two.
A paid promise is not the protective control.

steps.prompt: How do you address the card already opened?

choices.text: Dispute it with the issuer and relevant bureau, using the FTC recovery plan if appropriate.
choices.consequence: The existing record gets a specific challenge.
choices.explanation: A freeze alone does not delete old entries.

steps.prompt: The issuer asks for a case reference. What do you provide?

choices.text: A verified report/reference through the issuer's official process, retaining copies.
choices.consequence: The dispute has a traceable record.
choices.explanation: Share only requested information on a confirmed channel.

choices.text: Your full identity file through the repair ad's upload link.
choices.consequence: More sensitive data may be exposed.
choices.explanation: A third-party ad does not verify the issuer.

steps.prompt: A genuine loan application is due next month. What now?

choices.text: Plan a temporary lift at the bureau the lender uses, then restore the freeze.
choices.consequence: The legitimate check can proceed while protection resumes.
choices.explanation: A freeze is reversible; confirm the lender independently.

choices.text: Remove all freezes permanently because applications are impossible otherwise.

blocks.debrief: US freezes limit some new credit; disputes repair existing records. Local alternatives differ. Retry any choice and replay; do not enter real identity details into this exercise.

questions.prompt: Does a US credit freeze stop fraudulent use of an existing card?

choices.explanation: The freeze limits access to reports for new credit, not existing-card use.

choices.text: No; report existing-card misuse to the issuer separately.

questions.prompt: A Russian resident considers a consumer-loan self-ban. What limitation matters?

choices.text: It does not cover every credit product or existing card use.
choices.explanation: Bank of Russia lists exclusions and existing-card limits.

choices.text: It is identical to a US three-bureau freeze.

questions.prompt: Your own US mortgage lender cannot pull a report. What should you do?

choices.text: Verify the lender and temporarily lift the relevant freeze.
choices.explanation: The legitimate application can proceed without abandoning protection.

choices.text: Treat every failed pull as proof of identity theft.
choices.explanation: Your own freeze can explain it.
